messages.author: 5279e97a1a3d175c
messages.subject: Problems with the fitqtl() function
parts:
I have observed that the fitqtl() function occasionally gives me errors:

“Error in solve.default(t(Z) %*% Z, t(Z) %*% X)”

 

I am trying to fit a 1 QTL model, with the following code:

fitqtl(loc.data.sim, pheno.col=trt, qtl=qtl, method="imp", get.ests=TRUE, dropone=FALSE,model=model.type)

1 trait, 1 QTL, 1 position.

 

Any idea what the issue might be?

This is a F2 population, and the type of marker that I am analyzing with this fitQTL are the flanking markers of a QTL region.

The occurrence of the error is dataset dependent.

 

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problems with the fitqtl() function
parts:
Perhaps one of the genotypes at the QTL is not observed in your mapping population?

I'm not sure what you mean by "the type of marker...are the flanking markers of a QTL region".
Generally, I would include just one marker/position for each QTL.

karl

When the Error occurs I am fitting a single marker.

What I mean with “the type of marker...are the flanking markers of a QTL region” is:

That the error tends to occur when I fit a single marker that has been identified as flanking for a QTL region by using the LOD drop 2 method.

 

I will have a look at your suggestion regarding the missing genotype class.
